messages.author: 711ab6d699374ab7
messages.subject: Shinyapps is completely stupid
parts:
Hello,

I just wanted to upload an App to ShinyApps, but this is completely stupid. There is one easy way: upload your app (server, ui, plus files) via ftp/sftp, to your account, READY. Instead you choose to use something
shinyapps::setAccountInfo(name="<ACCOUNT>", token="<TOKEN>", secret="<SECRET>")
plus blablabllballblala
which a) does not work and b) is not documented c) far too complicated. I am really pissed and I am not willing to inform myself about the functionality of such a weird thing.

There remains only one question "WHY?".

Regards,
G

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shinyapps is completely stupid
parts:
Gunter,
Apologies that you have found ShinyApps so difficult to use.  The Platform as a service (PaaS) model is admittedly a newer paradigm that is not as well known in the industry yet.  If you are familiar with platforms like Heroku or CloudBees you can see other examples that compare to ShinyApps.  In the PaaS model, the service provider is taking care of providing you with self-contained computational resources based on your needs.   The developer can scale the resources up and down without needing to know about where the servers are hosted, how the code will be deployed and rolled out across the cluster etc...

Using an R package with semantics that are more familiar to R developers has made it easy for several hundred R developers to build an app and get it deployed within a short period of time.  It is different than a classic web hosting model, but we are hoping to learn through the alpha whether that is true or not.

If you would like to discuss this further, please don't hesitate to drop me a line.   We are using the alpha period to help us learn about what works and what doesn't and truly appreciate your feedback.

Best,
Tareef

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shinyapps is completely stupid
parts:
Our previous iteration of a hosting service, on the servers Glimmer and Spark, used a method similar to the one you describe. There are limitations with that system, with regard to user separation, resource allocation, software updates, package versioning, system maintenance, and scalability. As one example, those older hosting servers are still running R 2.15.3, because upgrading to R 3.0 will break the packages and apps for existing users. With ShinyApps, we're hoping to solve a lot of these issues.

-Winston
